consequence.statement: Policy exceptions are no longer enabled by default in all namespaces. Users who relied on that will see exceptions stop applying outside the namespaces they configure.
consequence.remediation: Explicitly configure the namespaces where policy exceptions should be enabled.

original.statement: The chart's default no longer enables policy exceptions in all namespaces (CVE-2024-48921), so users who relied on exceptions in all namespaces are affected.

consequence.statement: Users who relied on policy exceptions being allowed in all namespaces lose that after upgrading: exceptions configured outside the allowed namespace are no longer honoured. The upgrade guide lists this as a breaking change.
consequence.remediation: To keep allowing exceptions in all namespaces, set the Helm value features.policyExceptions.namespace to '*'. Limiting exceptions to a specific namespace is recommended instead, which means moving PolicyExceptions into that namespace.

corrected.statement: In Kyverno 1.13.0 the Helm chart no longer allows policy exceptions in all namespaces by default (CVE-2024-48921). Unless the operator sets features.policyExceptions.namespace to '*', exceptions they relied on in other namespaces are no longer honoured.

decision.reason: [ev-dea2079e5dc4] lists this under Breaking Changes: prior chart values enabled policy exceptions in all namespaces, and users relying on that are impacted. [ev-2bbc505de6bb] says that to "continue to allow configuring exceptions in all namespaces" the operator must set the Helm value `features.policyExceptions.namespace` to `*`. So if the operator does nothing, exceptions outside the allowed namespace stop being honoured. That is a failure kind (setting-ignored, which means mandatory work), not a behavior-change that keeps working; the proposed statement even says exceptions "stop applying", which contradicts its own kind.
